cause_quote: The new loopback bridge passed `requesterSenderId: undefined` to `acquireSessionMcpRuntime`, so requester-scoped servers were omitted even on turns with a verified sender.
user_saw: Users on managed Claude CLI turns could not see or use their per-requester MCP tools even after connecting their accounts.
summary: The fix exposes requester-scoped MCP tools through the Claude CLI loopback bridge, binds calls to the current verified sender, and gives senderless turns an explicit refusal.
reasoning: I checked the parent commit and found that restricted Claude CLI turns used a loopback catalog without configured MCP servers, while the native projection used operator OAuth credentials. PR #172026 introduced configured MCP support on the managed loopback path and omitted the requester from runtime acquisition from the start.
